name: USA
tagline: Skylines, canyons, coast roads — the widescreen country.
overview: America is where the movies were shot, and the déjà vu on arrival is real: yellow cabs streaming past Times Square, the Golden Gate half-dressed in fog, a first look into the Grand Canyon that no camera has ever honestly conveyed. The scale is the point and the problem — this is a country of trips, not a trip. First-timers do best pairing one coast with one wonder: New York with Niagara, or San Francisco with the national-parks loop through Yosemite and the canyon country, or Los Angeles with Vegas as the neon intermission. Internal flights and interstates make distance routine, tipping culture makes budgeting educational, and the B2 visa's interview wait makes early planning non-negotiable — start that process months out. What you get back is the density of icons: nowhere else stacks this many bucket-list frames, foods, skylines and landscapes inside one border.

quickFacts.timezone: GMT-5 to -8 · New York is 9½–10½ hrs behind IST
quickFacts.flightFromIndia: ≈15–16 hrs non-stop Delhi/Mumbai to New York; West Coast usually one stop
quickFacts.plug: Type A/B · 120V — Indian devices need an adapter, and check dual-voltage on appliances

visa.headline: B1/B2 visitor visa · start months early
visa.body: Indian passport holders need the B2 visitor visa: online DS-160, fee payment, then two appointments (biometrics and interview). Interview wait times at Indian consulates swing from weeks to many months, so begin the process the moment a trip becomes an idea. The visa, once granted, is typically valid ten years — the painful part pays off for a decade of trips.
visa.processing: Interview wait varies by city — check current estimates; the visa itself usually issues within days after

weather.summary: Every climate exists somewhere: New York does four sharp seasons, California coasts stay mild year-round, the desert Southwest bakes in summer, and Florida runs tropical with a hurricane season. The planning trick is regional — there's a perfect month for every route, and September–October comes closest to perfect everywhere at once.
weather.bestTime: May – June & September – October for most routes

seasons.label: Spring & fall
seasons.notes: The everywhere windows: parks open and temperate, cities walkable, October painting New England in fire colours.

seasons.label: High summer
seasons.notes: Road-trip season with school-holiday crowds; the coasts are glorious while Vegas and the canyons blast past 40°C.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.notes: New York under Christmas lights and January sales, ski season in the Rockies, Florida and California as warm escapes — but icy Northeast sidewalks and storm-prone flights.

booking.high: June – August, plus Thanksgiving and Christmas weeks
booking.low: Late January – early March & post-Labor Day September
booking.note: September is the connoisseur's month — summer weather, post-holiday hotel rates, national parks emptied of school traffic. Book park lodges (Yosemite, canyon rims) 6–12 months out; they sell before flights are even sensible to buy.

idealDuration.note: Ten nights pairs one coast with one wonder properly. A single week belongs to one region — New York alone can fill it without repeating a neighbourhood.

budget.note: Per person per day; New York and San Francisco hotels drive the top line. Remember the invisible 20–28%: taxes appear at checkout and tipping (18–20% at restaurants) is effectively mandatory — price menus accordingly.

safety.headline: Tourist America is broadly safe; neighbourhood awareness and health cover are the real briefing
tips: Travel insurance with high medical cover is non-negotiable — US healthcare bills are legendary, and an ER visit without cover can cost lakhs.
Neighbourhood character changes block to block in big cities; check areas before late-night walks and keep phones gripped on transit.
Never leave anything visible in parked cars — break-ins in San Francisco and LA are industrial-scale.
In national parks, heat and distance kill more visitors than wildlife: carry water in the desert, obey canyon-hike warnings, and store food properly in bear country.
If police stop your rental car, stay inside with hands visible on the wheel — protocol differs from India and matters.
Weather extremes are real: heed hurricane, tornado and winter-storm alerts, and build slack around winter Northeast flights.

goodToKnow: Tipping is the wage system, not a courtesy: 18–20% at sit-down restaurants, $1–2 per drink at bars, $2–5 per hotel-bag or housekeeping day.
Listed prices exclude tax — the checkout total always grows, everywhere, and it varies by state.
Distances demand flights: New York to LA is Delhi to London. Fly the long legs; drive only the scenic ones.
US-issued cards tap everywhere, and Indian contactless cards mostly work — but carry one backup card and some cash for diners and tolls.
CityPASS and park-entry bundles genuinely save: the $80 'America the Beautiful' annual pass covers every national park for a carload.
Portions are engineered for sharing — one main between two is a legitimate strategy, and 'to-go' boxes are standard.
Indian food is everywhere and often outstanding — Jackson Heights and Edison, NJ are pilgrimage-grade; vegetarian labelling is common in cities.
ESTA does not apply to Indian passports — the B2 visa interview is unavoidable, so start it before booking anything.

image.alt: The Grand Canyon's layers glowing at sunset

cities.name: Florida — Miami & Orlando
cities.blurb: Art-deco beachfront and Cuban coffee in Miami; Disney and Universal's theme-park universe in Orlando — America's family-holiday engine room.

image.alt: Art-deco facades along Miami's Ocean Drive

highlights.name: Times Square & a Broadway night
highlights.blurb: The world's brightest intersection, then the world's best musical theatre two blocks away — New York doing what only New York can.
highlights.detail: Times Square is best treated as a fifteen-minute immersion — step in, let the billboards wash over you, then spend the evening properly: at a Broadway show. Book hit shows weeks ahead on official sites; for spontaneity, the TKTS booth under the red steps sells same-day seats at up to half price, and digital lotteries offer $40-ish tickets to even the biggest titles. Matinees cost less than Friday nights. The square itself peaks twice — full neon around 8pm, and near-empty at 6am, when photographers finally win. Dinner move: skip the square's chain restaurants for Hell's Kitchen's Ninth Avenue, five minutes west.

image.alt: Broadway marquees lit along a Manhattan street

highlights.name: Grand Canyon's South Rim
highlights.blurb: 277 miles long, a mile deep, and completely unphotographable in the good way — sunrise at Mather Point recalibrates you.
highlights.detail: The South Rim is the classic for reasons: open year-round, dense with viewpoints, and served by free shuttles along Hermit Road. See it twice daily — sunrise at Mather or Yaki Point, sunset at Hopi Point — because the canyon is really a light show performed on rock. Walk a stretch of the flat Rim Trail between shuttle stops to lose the crowds instantly. Descending even a mile into the canyon on Bright Angel Trail changes the scale entirely; descending far without a plan is how rescues happen — down takes twice the effort back up. Book rim lodges nearly a year out, or Tusayan and Williams as fallbacks. Vegas helicopters serve the West Rim's Skywalk — a different, further section.

image.alt: Dawn light filling the Grand Canyon from Mather Point

highlights.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
highlights.blurb: The harbour icon and the hall where twelve million arrivals became Americans — one ferry, two chapters of the national story.
highlights.detail: Only Statue City Cruises from Battery Park is the real ferry — ignore the costumed ticket hustlers along the waterfront. Book weeks ahead for pedestal access, months for the crown's 162-spiral-stair climb; general grounds tickets still deliver the classic angles. The under-visited half is Ellis Island: the Registry Room where steamship arrivals queued for new lives, and archives where visitors trace ancestors. Take the first morning boat — security lines compound through the day. The zero-dollar alternative every guidebook whispers: the Staten Island Ferry crosses the harbour past the statue, free, 24 hours a day, with the skyline as the return show.

image.alt: The Statue of Liberty above New York Harbor

highlights.name: Golden Gate Bridge by bike
highlights.blurb: Ride the great red span from the marina to Sausalito's waterfront, then ferry home past Alcatraz — San Francisco's perfect half-day.
highlights.detail: The classic loop: rent bikes at Fisherman's Wharf, roll through Crissy Field's beach paths, climb to the bridge deck and cross 2.7 km of international orange with the Pacific on one side and the bay on the other. Descend into Sausalito for waterfront lunch, then let the ferry do the return — it slides past Alcatraz with the skyline stacking up ahead, the best ₹1,200 cruise in California. Fog is a character, not a spoiler: summer mornings often hide the towers until noon, September–October run clearest. Viewpoint hierarchy for photographers: Battery Spencer above the north tower at golden hour beats everything.

image.query: golden gate bridge bike crissy field
image.alt: Cyclists approaching the Golden Gate Bridge

highlights.name: Yosemite Valley
highlights.blurb: El Capitan's kilometre of granite, Yosemite Falls at full spring thunder, and Tunnel View's curtain-raise — the national-park idea, perfected.
highlights.detail: Four hours from San Francisco, the valley arrival through Tunnel View is American scenery's single greatest reveal: El Capitan left, Bridalveil Fall right, Half Dome floating behind. Spring (May–June) is the waterfall season — Yosemite Falls dries to a stain by late summer. The valley floor's loop road and shuttle serve the icons easily; the Mist Trail to Vernal Fall is the essential half-day hike, wet and worth it. Summer entries may require timed reservations — check ahead — and valley lodging books out nearly a year early, with Curry Village's tent cabins as the accessible fallback. Watch El Capitan's face at dusk through binoculars: the moving lights are climbers settling in for the night.

image.alt: Yosemite Valley from Tunnel View with El Capitan

highlights.name: Niagara Falls
highlights.blurb: Three-quarters of a million gallons a second — felt from a boat deck in a complimentary poncho.
highlights.detail: The falls straddle the border, and honesty requires saying it: the postcard panorama belongs to the Canadian side, so Indians holding a Canadian visa should walk across the Rainbow Bridge for an afternoon. The American side counters with proximity — Cave of the Winds' wooden decks put you inside Bridal Veil Falls' spray zone, and the Maid of the Mist boat (running since 1846) drives straight at the Horseshoe's curtain until the world turns white noise. Evening illuminations and summer fireworks reward an overnight stay over the standard day-trip. From New York City it's an hour's flight to Buffalo; the eight-hour drive is for committed road-trippers only.

image.query: niagara falls maid of the mist
image.alt: The Maid of the Mist beneath Niagara's Horseshoe Falls

highlights.name: Antelope Canyon & Horseshoe Bend
highlights.blurb: Sandstone corridors carved into light-beam cathedrals, and the Colorado wrapping a 270° meander — Page, Arizona's double bill.
highlights.detail: Antelope Canyon sits on Navajo land and is visitable only with Navajo guides — book Upper Canyon's late-morning slots (roughly 10am–1pm) for the famous light beams, which are a summer phenomenon; Lower Canyon offers ladders, fewer crowds and equal beauty. Photography rules change seasonally; guides know every angle and will literally pose your camera. Ten minutes away, Horseshoe Bend asks a 2.4 km round-trip walk to an unfenced rim 300 metres above the Colorado's perfect curve — sunset colours it best, wind demands respect at the edge. Page slots naturally between the Grand Canyon and Monument Valley on the great Southwest loop.

image.alt: A light beam striking the sandstone curves of Antelope Canyon

highlights.name: Orlando's theme-park universe
highlights.blurb: Disney's four kingdoms and Universal's Wizarding World — engineered joy at a scale no other place attempts.
highlights.detail: Orlando is a logistics game with a magical prize. Pick a lane rather than exhausting the family: Magic Kingdom plus Hollywood Studios for Disney's core (fireworks over the castle remain undefeated), or Universal's two parks linked by the Hogwarts Express for Potter pilgrims — riding between Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade requires the two-park ticket and justifies it. Use the official apps obsessively: virtual queues, Lightning Lane/Express Pass purchases and dining reservations decide whether the day averages 4 rides or 12. September and late January bring the shortest lines. Build a pool-day between park days; the Florida sun and the mileage are real.

image.alt: Fireworks over Cinderella Castle at Walt Disney World

highlights.name: Pacific Coast Highway — Big Sur
highlights.blurb: Highway 1 clinging to cliffs between Monterey and San Simeon: Bixby Bridge, McWay's beach waterfall, condors overhead.
highlights.detail: The Big Sur stretch is the American drive: 145 km where the road becomes a balcony over the Pacific. Drive southbound so the ocean rides your window, and let the icons pace you — Bixby Creek Bridge's concrete arch, Pfeiffer Beach's purple sand and keyhole rock, McWay Falls dropping 25 metres onto a cove you admire from above, and elephant seals hauled out near San Simeon. Fuel up in Monterey or Carmel (Big Sur's lone pumps charge collector prices), check Caltrans for slide closures — the cliffs periodically reclaim the road — and book the area's few lodgings early. Two days beats one; sunset at Nepenthe's terrace is the classic close.

image.alt: Bixby Bridge arching over the Big Sur coastline

highlights.name: Washington's National Mall
highlights.blurb: The Smithsonian's free museum mile between the Capitol and Lincoln's marble gaze — democracy's front lawn, admission ₹0.
highlights.detail: Nowhere else stacks this much, free: Air and Space's actual Wright Flyer and Apollo capsules, Natural History's Hope Diamond, the National Gallery, and the American History museum's cultural attic — every Smithsonian is $0, every day. Thread them along the two-mile Mall walk from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial, detouring to the Vietnam and Korean memorials, with the Washington Monument as the constant compass needle. The African American History museum still requires timed passes — reserve ahead. Evening changes the register: the memorials floodlit and near-empty after 8pm are the capital's most moving hours. Three hours from New York by train, and worth two full days.

image.alt: The Lincoln Memorial mirrored in the Reflecting Pool

trips.title: New York & the East
trips.summary: Five Manhattan nights done properly — Liberty ferry, Broadway, Central Park, one borough food crawl — then Niagara's spray and the capital's free museum mile. The classic first America, walkable and train-linked once you land.

image.alt: Central Park's trees against the midtown skyline

trips.title: California & the canyons
trips.summary: The great western loop: Golden Gate by bike, Yosemite's valley, the Vegas intermission, then Antelope Canyon, Horseshoe Bend and the South Rim before an LA finale. One rental car, the full American widescreen — September does it best.

image.alt: The road into Yosemite Valley beneath granite walls

trips.title: Orlando & Miami family run
trips.summary: Six park-strategy days across Disney and Universal — Potter, fireworks, one pool-day breather — then Miami's South Beach warm-down with a Everglades airboat morning. The family blockbuster, engineered to end relaxed instead of exhausted.

faqs.q: How long does the US visa really take for Indians?
faqs.a: The B2's bottleneck is the interview appointment — waits at Indian consulates have ranged from a few weeks to many months, shifting constantly. Start the DS-160 and book the interview the moment a trip becomes an idea; once interviewed, passports typically return within days, and the visa usually runs ten years.

faqs.q: East coast or west coast first?
faqs.a: New York for the city-and-icons trip — it's the denser, easier logistics. The West for landscapes: San Francisco, Yosemite, Vegas and the canyons chain into the world's best road-trip loop. With 12+ nights, one internal flight buys you both.

It's the service wage: 18–20% at any sit-down restaurant (some bills add it automatically — check), $1–2 per bar drink, a few dollars daily for housekeeping, 15–20% on taxis and salons. Counter service is genuinely optional. Budget it as a real 20% on food from day one.

faqs.q: Is the US doable on a budget?
faqs.a: Yes, with structure: motels and chain hotels outside downtown cores, supermarket breakfasts, the $80 annual parks pass, free icons (Staten Island Ferry, National Mall, Golden Gate) and one splurge per city. New York and San Francisco will still tax the wallet — balance them with park days.

Among the easiest Western countries: every city has serious Indian restaurants (Jackson Heights, NY and Edison, NJ are destination-grade), chains label vegetarian clearly, and Mexican, Italian and Mediterranean menus fill any gaps. Even highway stops manage veggie burgers now.
